items.q: 25 cm³ of 0,1 mol·dm⁻³ HCl is neutralised by NaOH. How many moles of NaOH react? (HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O)
items.qAf: 25 cm³ van 0,1 mol·dm⁻³ HCl word deur NaOH geneutraliseer. Hoeveel mol NaOH reageer? (HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O)
items.explain: n(HCl) = c × V = 0,1 × 0,025 = 0,0025 mol. The mole ratio is 1 : 1, so n(NaOH) = 0,0025 mol.
items.explainAf: n(HCl) = c × V = 0,1 × 0,025 = 0,0025 mol. Die molverhouding is 1 : 1, dus n(NaOH) = 0,0025 mol.

items.q: In a titration, 20 cm³ of NaOH (0,2 mol·dm⁻³) requires 10 cm³ of H₂SO₄ to neutralise (2NaOH + H₂SO₄ → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O). What is the concentration of H₂SO₄?
items.qAf: In ’n titrasie benodig 20 cm³ NaOH (0,2 mol·dm⁻³) 10 cm³ H₂SO₄ om te neutraliseer (2NaOH + H₂SO₄ → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O). Wat is die konsentrasie van H₂SO₄?
items.explain: n(NaOH) = 0,2 × 0,020 = 0,004 mol. The ratio is 2 : 1, so n(H₂SO₄) = 0,002 mol. V = 10 cm³ = 0,010 dm³, so c = 0,002 ÷ 0,010 = 0,2 mol·dm⁻³.
items.explainAf: n(NaOH) = 0,2 × 0,020 = 0,004 mol. Die verhouding is 2 : 1, dus is n(H₂SO₄) = 0,002 mol. V = 10 cm³ = 0,010 dm³, dus c = 0,002 ÷ 0,010 = 0,2 mol·dm⁻³.

items.q: The end point of a titration is reached when:
items.qAf: Die eindpunt van ’n titrasie word bereik wanneer:
items.explain: The indicator's colour change shows the equivalence point has been reached.
items.explainAf: Die indikator se kleurverandering wys dat die ekwivalensiepunt bereik is.

items.q: How many grams of water form from 2 mol H₂ and excess O₂? (2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, M(H₂O) = 18 g·mol⁻¹)
items.qAf: Hoeveel gram water vorm uit 2 mol H₂ en oormaat O₂? (2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, M(H₂O) = 18 g·mol⁻¹)
items.explain: 2 mol H₂ gives 2 mol H₂O = 2 × 18 = 36 g.
items.explainAf: 2 mol H₂ gee 2 mol H₂O = 2 × 18 = 36 g.

items.q: 4 mol H₂ reacts with 1 mol O₂ (2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O). Which reactant is limiting and how many moles of water form?
items.qAf: 4 mol H₂ reageer met 1 mol O₂ (2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O). Watter reaktant is beperkend en hoeveel mol water vorm?
items.explain: 1 mol O₂ needs 2 mol H₂, so O₂ is limiting. It forms 2 mol H₂O.
items.explainAf: 1 mol O₂ benodig 2 mol H₂, dus is O₂ beperkend. Dit vorm 2 mol H₂O.

items.q: The limiting reagent is the reactant that:
items.qAf: Die beperkende reaktant is die reaktant wat:
options: is used up first and limits the product
optionsAf: eerste opgebruik word en die produk beperk
items.explain: Once the limiting reagent is used up, the reaction stops, so it sets the maximum yield.
items.explainAf: Sodra die beperkende reaktant opgebruik is, stop die reaksie, dus bepaal dit die maksimum opbrengs.

items.q: The reactant that is used up first and so limits the amount of product.
items.qAf: Die reaktant wat eerste opgebruik word en dus die hoeveelheid produk beperk.

items.q: The point in a titration where the acid and base have reacted completely in the mole ratio of the equation.
items.qAf: Die punt in ’n titrasie waar die suur en basis volledig in die molverhouding van die vergelyking gereageer het.

items.q: The actual yield as a percentage of the theoretical yield.
items.qAf: Die werklike opbrengs as ’n persentasie van die teoretiese opbrengs.

items.q: A solution of exactly known concentration.

items.text: In a titration, the solution of known concentration is usually in the [[]], and an [[]] shows the end point by changing colour.
items.textAf: In ’n titrasie is die oplossing van bekende konsentrasie gewoonlik in die [[]], en ’n [[]] wys die eindpunt deur van kleur te verander.

items.q: At STP, 2 mol of oxygen gas occupies 44,8 dm³.
items.qAf: By STD beslaan 2 mol suurstofgas 44,8 dm³.

items.q: 25 cm³ of 0,1 mol/dm³ NaOH exactly neutralises 20 cm³ of HCl. Calculate the concentration of the HCl in mol/dm³.
items.qAf: 25 cm³ van 0,1 mol/dm³ NaOH neutraliseer presies 20 cm³ HCl. Bereken die konsentrasie van die HCl in mol/dm³.

items.q: The theoretical yield of a reaction is 50 g but only 40 g is obtained. Calculate the percentage yield.
items.qAf: Die teoretiese opbrengs van ’n reaksie is 50 g maar net 40 g word verkry. Bereken die persentasie-opbrengs.
